criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`: a new test where an item on a line that is neither paused nor flagged fails twice and the batch then runs the next item to completion (for example it lands). The test asserts the report has no repeated-failure stop and records the failed item as passed over, with a reason.
criteria.evidence: I ran the new test `an_item_that_fails_twice_on_an_unflagged_unpaused_line_is_passed_over_and_the_next_item_runs` (tests/drain.rs:911) and it passes. Its setup has no paused or flagged line, and the outcomes are Rejected, Rejected, Landed. It checks: the log goes read a, run a, reread a, run a-retry, read b, run b, land b, rate; the stop is QueueEmpty; landed == 1; b's job line is passed/landed; a's two job lines are kept; exactly one line reads `plan       a passed over: failed twice; left for the scope guard and Hestia: ended rejected`, printed after 2 runs; and display::drain does not contain 'repeated failure'. The sibling fails_twice tests also pass (4 of 4). On the base code, the old `ItemEnd::Failed => set_stop(RepeatedFailure)` arm would end the log after run a-retry. Athena's fails-without run did not compile, because other new tests use Stop::Environment.

summary: The change does what was asked. In drain.rs, an item that fails twice on a line that is neither paused nor flagged no longer stops the batch. It is passed over with the reason `failed twice; left for the scope guard and Hestia: <reason>`, its failed job lines stay in the report, and the next item runs. The stop is removed where it was set (the `ItemEnd::Failed` arm), not special-cased for one job, so this fixes the root cause. Before, the only way a batch stopped on an expired login was the repeated-failure stop, so the change adds an `environment` stop. It fires only when the second failure's closing reason is an expired login, a usage limit or low disk; tests show a check timeout and a plain work failure do not stop the batch. The disk-hold, settings/reinstall, kill-switch, budget and job-limit stops are kept. Their tests lost only assertions about the removed stop and field. I ran the new pass-over test, the login, usage-limit, disk and timeout tests, the help test and the stop-label unit test, and all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. The help text, display, module docs, README and CHANGELOG (which names job 20261029-160024-80qj and the 4 Nov stop) are updated. Minor findings only: README.md and tests/job_plan.rs are outside the listed deliverables but are needed; docs/spec.toml:1351 still says a repeated failure stops the drain; and the `--json` shape changed, which the CHANGELOG states.
